components.name: Multi-factor authentication
components.technology: privacyIDEA TOTP/push via its PAM module on the SSH bastion and its FreeRADIUS plugin on the VPN; administrators additionally use FIDO2 OpenSSH keys (ed25519-sk); per-source-IP lockout at 10 failures / 5 min
components.why: Preventive: stops a guessed password from becoming a session; it would have blocked the 09:04 login.

components.name: Network segmentation
components.technology: OPNsense firewall, VLANs, default-deny inter-zone rules, egress allow-list proxy, quarantine VLAN
components.why: Preventive by design: 10.20.4.15 reaches RS-01 only through the bastion and unknown egress (09:13) is denied. Its quarantine VLAN is reused for containment in recovery step 2.

components.name: Privileged access management
components.technology: Just-in-time sudo, separate admin accounts, no standing root, agent tamper protection
components.why: Preventive: backup deletion (09:12) and disabling antivirus (09:18) need a just-in-time approval the attacker does not have.

components.name: Monitoring / SIEM
components.technology: Wazuh SIEM + Prometheus/Grafana, correlation rules, active response
components.why: Detective: raises the 09:01 and 09:07 alerts. Its active response only orchestrates; the hypervisor, firewall and identity provider carry out the containment.

components.name: Intrusion detection
components.technology: Suricata NIDS, Wazuh HIDS/FIM with canary files and an extension/entropy check, AI anomaly scorer
components.why: Detective: detects the encryption (09:07) and the unknown outbound connection (09:13).

components.name: Immutable backup
components.technology: Tier 1 (fast restore): ZFS snapshots every 3 min on RS-01, pulled by the vault (zfs send -i | zfs receive, initiated from the vault) into its own pool and held with zfs hold; PostgreSQL WAL pulled continuously by pg_receivewal on the vault plus a nightly base backup. Tier 2 (WORM): restic copies every 15 min into a MinIO bucket with S3 Object Lock in compliance mode (30 days). Production holds no vault credentials
components.why: Recovery against ransomware: it does not stop encryption, but keeps clean restore points out of the attacker's reach. Tier 1 (worst-case loss 4 min) is protected by credential separation and zfs hold; tier 2 is write-once even for a vault administrator.

components.name: Secure failover
components.technology: Research-Server-02: warm VM cloned from a golden image, holds no data and waits in the isolated recovery VLAN, out of reach of an attacker in the research VLAN; promoted after verification by re-tagging its vNIC into the research VLAN and switching the service VIP/DNS
components.why: Recovery: restores service on clean infrastructure within the RTO and never receives live-replicated (encrypted) data.
components.zone: Recovery zone (isolated VLAN; moved into the research VLAN on promotion)

components.name: Recovery environment
components.technology: Isolated clean-room VLAN without internet access: restore, scan, verify
components.why: Recovery: restored data is verified in isolation before it returns to production.

components.name: Virtualisation host (hypervisor)
components.technology: VM cluster running RS-01 and RS-02; its API lets Wazuh active response pause a VM, re-tag its vNIC into the quarantine VLAN and take memory + disk snapshots for evidence
components.why: Response point, listed with recovery because the template has no respond column: containment and evidence capture happen here, since VLAN membership is set on the vNIC, not on the firewall.

components.name: Offline copy at a second Kazakhstan site
components.technology: Logically air-gapped copy in Almaty (~970 km from Astana): transfer window opened daily from the Almaty side only, monthly rotation to disconnected media, separate admin domain, monthly restore drill; data-loss tier 24 h
components.why: Recovery: last resort that survives compromise of the vault's admin plane or loss of the Astana site.

threat_controls.detective: SIEM alert at ≥10 failures / 5 min per source; "success after failures" correlation
threat_controls.preventive: MFA on the bastion and VPN; per-source-IP lockout at 10 failures / 5 min (per IP, not per account, so attackers cannot lock researchers out); SSH unreachable from the user VLAN
threat_controls.recovery: Respond: block the source, revoke sessions. Recover: rotate the password, re-enrol MFA, review account activity

threat_controls.detective: Canary-file write (immediate); FIM rate ≥100 changes/min AND extension/entropy change; CPU >90% and AI score used only as correlating signals
threat_controls.preventive: Segmentation; least-privilege write access to research shares; noexec on /tmp, /dev/shm and user-writable mounts plus application allow-listing (fapolicyd)
threat_controls.recovery: Respond: the hypervisor pauses RS-01 and moves it into the quarantine VLAN. Recover: restore data from the verified clean point onto RS-02, verify it in the clean room, then promote RS-02

threat_controls.detective: Alert on any delete or retention-change API call, or a failed vault login
threat_controls.preventive: Pull-only vault, so production holds no vault credentials; zfs hold on vault snapshots; Object Lock compliance mode on the restic tier; just-in-time admin
threat_controls.recovery: Recover: restore from the vault (tier 1, then the Object Lock tier); the offline Almaty copy is the last resort

threat_controls.detective: Suricata alert on a non-allow-listed destination and on volume anomalies; database query-rate anomaly
threat_controls.preventive: Egress default-deny allow-list proxy; least-privilege database roles
threat_controls.recovery: Respond: block the destination, revoke database credentials. Recover: scope the leaked records, report to KZ-CERT, and notify the authorised personal-data body and data subjects where Law No. 94-V and university policy require it

threat_controls.detective: Alert on AV/EDR stop, a new admin account, or sudo outside the just-in-time window
threat_controls.preventive: Just-in-time admin, no standing root, agent tamper protection
threat_controls.recovery: Recover: rebuild the host from a golden image in the clean room; rotate all privileged credentials

events.attack_ref: T1589 Gather Victim Identity Information (tactic: Reconnaissance)
events.evidence: First contact from 10.20.4.15: 15 failed logins in the first logged burst (Medium severity). Consistent with probing which usernames exist and whether lockout is enforced.
21 more failed logins from the same source 10.20.4.15; 36 cumulative failures logged between 09:01 and 09:03.
Successful login from 10.20.4.15 immediately after 36 failed attempts (first failure logged 09:01): a guessed password became a valid session.

events.attack_ref: T1486 Data Encrypted for Impact (tactic: Impact)
events.evidence: 320 files modified by the attacker session (source 10.20.4.15), 3 min after the successful login.

events.alternative: 95% CPU alone is not specific on a research server (see Part E); resource hijacking (T1496) is less likely given the timing.
events.attack_ref: T1486 Data Encrypted for Impact (tactic: Impact)
events.evidence: CPU at 95% on Research-Server-01, 1 min after the 320 file modifications and 2 min before 1,200 files are reported encrypted, so consistent with the encryption workload.

events.attack_ref: T1486 Data Encrypted for Impact (tactic: Impact)
events.evidence: 1,200 files encrypted on Research-Server-01: direct loss of research data.
Backup deletion attempt on Research-Server-01, 2 min after encryption: an attack on the ability to recover.

events.alternative: A command-and-control channel only; double extortion is a hypothesis.
events.attack_ref: T1041 Exfiltration Over C2 Channel (tactic: Exfiltration)
events.evidence: Outbound connection from Research-Server-01 to an unknown IP. No transfer volume is logged, so exfiltration is assessed, not confirmed.

events.attack_ref: TA0008 Lateral Movement (assumed T1021 Remote Services, RS-01 → DB) + T1213 Data from Information Repositories (tactic: Collection)
events.evidence: Database access spike from Research-Server-01: the compromised server is used as a pivot into the research database. Stated assumption: the database runs on a separate host. The queries may feed the outbound channel opened at 09:13.

events.alternative: Defense evasion; the spec vocabulary has no such stage, so it is classed as persistence.
events.attack_ref: T1562.001 Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools (tactic: Defense Evasion)
events.evidence: Antivirus disabled on Research-Server-01 at 09:18, 8 min after 1,200 files were encrypted. The dataset shows no AV alert during 09:07–09:10, so AV did not stop the encryption. Disabling it protects the attacker's continued access and hampers forensics.

steps.component: ids + monitoring (canary / FIM + entropy rule, SIEM correlation, AI score)
steps.details: Canary write or FIM rate + entropy rule fires on the 09:07 mass modification; Wazuh correlates it with the 09:01 brute-force alert and the AI score.

steps.component: hypervisor (VM pause, vNIC into the quarantine VLAN) + segmentation (OPNsense deny rule) + privacyIDEA/IdP (account lock), triggered by Wazuh active response
steps.details: Automated: the hypervisor pauses RS-01 (memory preserved) and re-tags its vNIC into the quarantine VLAN, OPNsense blocks 10.20.4.15 and RS-01's address, and privacyIDEA locks the compromised account.

steps.component: hypervisor (VM memory + disk snapshot) + monitoring (SIEM log export, SHA-256, WORM bucket)
steps.details: Snapshot the paused VM's memory and disk, export SIEM/FIM/Suricata logs, hash everything with SHA-256 and store it in a write-once bucket.

steps.component: immutable_backup (choose the clean point, clone it read-only from the vault ZFS pool into the clean room)
steps.details: Choose the clean point before restoring: diff the 09:06 snapshot against 09:03 (new executables, authorized_keys or cron entries, changed canaries). Use 09:06 if the diff is clean, otherwise 09:03 (before attacker access), and clone it read-only into the recovery environment.

steps.component: failover (RS-02 warm VM from a golden image; data copied from the clean point; PostgreSQL PITR)
steps.details: Copy data from the clean point onto RS-02 (assumption: ≤200 GB over 10 GbE ≈ 3 min) and run PostgreSQL point-in-time recovery to the clean point (≤5 min) unless the DB audit log shows an earlier malicious write.

steps.component: recovery_env (hash manifest, YARA/AV scan, persistence check, DB consistency, canaries intact)
steps.details: Compare file hashes with the clean-point manifest, scan with YARA/AV, confirm no new executables, authorized_keys or cron entries, run DB consistency checks and confirm the canary files are intact.

steps.component: failover + hypervisor (RS-02 vNIC into the research VLAN, VIP/DNS switch, rotated credentials)
steps.details: Promote RS-02: re-tag its vNIC from the recovery VLAN into the research VLAN, switch the service VIP/DNS, rotate credentials and keep heightened monitoring; only after the evidence is preserved and integrity is verified.

risk.impact_rule: Impact 5 = loss of research data or of the ability to recover; 4 = serious but bounded (access or confidentiality).
risk.likelihood_rule: Likelihood 5 = observed and succeeded in this incident; 4 = attempted or indirectly evidenced, with the outcome not logged.

threats.impact_reason: I4: it grants entry to the research server but is not damage by itself.
threats.likelihood_reason: L5 (observed and succeeded): the 09:04 login succeeded after 36 guesses against password-only access.

threats.impact_reason: I5: loss of research data and of the server's availability.
threats.likelihood_reason: L5 (observed and succeeded): 1,200 files were encrypted by 09:10.

threats.impact_reason: I5: it removes recoverability, turning a recoverable incident into permanent loss.
threats.likelihood_reason: L4 (attempted, outcome not logged): a deletion attempt at 09:12 against mutable backups, by an attacker who already held the rights it needs.

threats.impact_reason: I4: confidentiality loss of research and personal data with legal exposure, but no data destroyed.
threats.likelihood_reason: L4 (indirectly evidenced): an outbound connection to an unknown IP (09:13) and a database spike within 2 min (09:15), with no transfer volume logged.

threats.impact_reason: I4: an enabler of the other threats rather than damage by itself.
threats.likelihood_reason: L4 (indirectly evidenced): disabling antivirus and deleting backups both require administrative rights.
